summary.summary: This is Cyngor Gwynedd's own 2025/26 Statement of Accounts, still marked 'Subject to Audit', going to the council's Governance and Audit Committee. The balance sheet is solid: long-term borrowing fell from £90.1m to £69.4m over the year, total reserves grew from £592.7m to £644.6m, and the unearmarked General Fund balance nearly doubled from £7.9m to £14.5m after a deliberate top-up. The Capital Financing Requirement rose to £188.5m (from £179.9m) even as external borrowing fell, meaning the council is increasingly relying on internal borrowing rather than new external debt. The narrative notes real budget pressure — a £6.6m in-year overspend concentrated in adult/children's care and waste — but there is no exceptional financial support, capitalisation direction, or section 114-type language anywhere in the document.

news_drafts.headline: Gwynedd took out no new loans in first quarter of 2026/27, leaving borrowing at £73.9m
news_drafts.lead:
Gwynedd Council took out no new loans in the first quarter of 2026/27, and its total borrowing stood at £73.9m, unchanged from 31 March. The figures are in the treasury management update (the report on how the council borrows and invests its spare cash) that went to its Governance and Audit Committee on 29 September.

The council says this is deliberate. It is using what is known as internal borrowing, meaning it pays for long-lasting spending from its own cash rather than taking a loan. This saves interest but uses up the cash cushion. The paper says the approach keeps borrowing below the council's underlying need.

The paper says the strategy "enabled the Council to reduce net borrowing costs (despite foregoing investment income) and reduce overall treasury risk". In other words, cash that is spent in place of a loan no longer earns interest as an investment, but the council judges the interest it saves on loans to be worth more. Its net investments stood at £11.4m.

findings.committee: North Wales CJC Economic Well-being Sub-committee
findings.paper_title: 2026/27 Revenue and Capital Position - End of July 2026 Review
findings.headline: Portfolio Management Office recorded £680,896 underspend, with £586,668 in staff costs shifted to project-level and grant funding.
findings.detail: £348,000 of staff costs are now funded by Ambition North Wales's Growth Deal projects, £121,000 by grants (Local Area Energy Plan and Shared Prosperity Fund), and vacant posts contributed over £60,000. This shows flexible funding models but also indicates staffing gaps during the year.
findings.matters: Reveals how staffing is actually distributed across projects rather than held at PMO level; peer councils track whether delivery capacity was fully deployed.
findings.figures: £680,896 PMO underspend; £586,668 employee expenditure variance; £348,000 Ambition North Wales funding; £121,000 grant funding; ~£60,000 vacancies
findings.quote: The underspend on the employee expenditure heading is £586,668 and this is due to some staff costs that were included within the core budget were subsequently funded by other sources. Around £348,000 of the underspend is due to staff that are now funded by Ambition North Wales's Growth Deal projects... These grants were therefore used to fund staff costs, which together contribute to around £121,000 of the underspend. Vacant posts during the year also led to a further underspend of over £60,000 in employee expenditure.

findings.committee: North Wales CJC Economic Well-being Sub-committee
findings.paper_title: 2026/27 Revenue and Capital Position - End of July 2026 Review
findings.headline: Investment Zone achieving neutral budget position by using £227,589 of interest income alongside £200,000 grant allocation.
findings.detail: Interest on retained grant balances is being deployed to bridge the gap between allocated funding and forecast expenditure, achieving a neutral year-end position. This approach is explicitly described as temporary; the CJC notes that interest income will decline as cash outflows from grant distribution accelerate.
findings.matters: The underlying cost structure exceeds sustainable grant funding; reliance on interest income is time-limited and signals an emerging funding gap as balances decline.
findings.figures: £227,589 interest income used; £200,000 annual grant allocation
findings.quote: In order to leave a neutral position for the Investment Zone, interest from the Investment Zone grant balances of £227,589 will be used, in addition to the £200,000 grant allocation. The use of interest is a temporary arrangement as the cash outflows from distributing the Investment Zone grant will reduce the interest income.

findings.committee: North Wales CJC Economic Well-being Sub-committee
findings.paper_title: 2026/27 Revenue and Capital Position - End of July 2026 Review
findings.headline: Growth Deal revenue budget forecast to underspend by £288,174 in 2026/27.
findings.detail: Underspend is primarily from vacant posts and staff costs being funded from other sources, including Ambition North Wales projects, Local Area Energy Plan and Shared Prosperity Fund grants. The underspend will be carried forward to fund future budgets and reduce future partner contribution increases.
findings.matters: Demonstrates budget control and signals potential reduction in future funding pressures from partner councils.
findings.quote: It is estimated that the net out-turn position at the end of the 2026/27 financial year will be an underspend of £288,174. This is mainly due to underspends in employee expenditure, additional government roles, accountable body support services and external legal, finance and procurement support. An underspend at the end of the financial year will be used to fund future budgets and reduce any increases in future partner contributions.

findings.committee: North Wales CJC Economic Well-being Sub-committee
findings.paper_title: 2026/27 Revenue and Capital Position - End of July 2026 Review
findings.headline: Growth Deal capital expenditure forecast at £51.26m against approved budget of £67.07m, a reduction of £15.81m due to project slippage.
findings.detail: Capital spending is expected to underspend by £15.81m (23.6%) in 2026/27. Although the Business Gateway project introduction and brought-forward Reserve List projects have partially offset the slippage, project delivery delays remain substantial.
findings.matters: Material capital variance signals delivery risk; lenders and peer finance directors track whether councils are executing capital programmes as planned.
findings.quote: There is a net reduction of £15.81m in the anticipated expenditure for 2026/27 and this is due to slippage on projects. However, the introduction of the Business Gateway project in the capital profile and the brought forward expenditure on the Reserve List projects have reduced the slippage.

findings.headline: Ombudsman complaints increased despite overall formal complaint numbers falling
findings.detail: The council saw formal complaints decrease overall, but those escalated to Ombudsman increased. This suggests that complaints being made are either more serious or less resolvable through council processes.
findings.matters: Rising Ombudsman escalations can indicate either deteriorating service quality or poor complaint resolution, both affecting reputation and potentially generating costs.
findings.quote: The number of Valid Formal Complaints has decreased this year compared to last year, but those that have gone to the Ombudsman have increased.
